findings.title: `"Not tucked"` styling pill generated when layering a sweater over a dress
findings.evidence: **Eva (`01:02`):** `"Glede na to, da je pulover čez obleko, ga zelo težko zatakneš... mogoče je tle mišljeno, da oblečeš pulover čez oblekco, kar je dejansko ful dobra ideja"` `[Screen: Today outfit shows white sweater + floral dress with note "Wear it with the white top left untucked over the black dress" and pill "Not tucked".]`
findings.current: When AI suggests layering a sweater/pullover over a dress on `Today`, it attaches the `"Not tucked"` pill and `"left untucked"` styling note.
findings.expected: Suppress `"Not tucked"` / `"tucked"` styling tags when a top/knitwear piece is layered over a dress or jumpsuit.

findings.title: Swap or lock individual pieces on `Today` outfit suggestion instead of regenerating entire look
findings.evidence: **Eva (`01:28`–`01:55`):** `"Mogoče na tej točki bi jaz želela imeti opcijo, da bi lahko zamenjala samo čevlje, ali pa samo pulover... da obdržim obleko pa pulover, pa zamenjam čevlje."` `[Screen: Tapping the sweater opens item detail; tapping "Try another" regenerates the whole outfit.]`
findings.current: `Today` only offers `"Try another"`, which replaces every item in the suggested outfit at once.
findings.expected: Allow locking/keeping specific pieces or swapping a single piece (e.g., just shoes or just top) within a `Today` outfit recommendation.

findings.title: Unclear purpose of `"Wear this"` / `"Wearing today"` button on `Today`
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva.styld1.mp4` `02:24`):** `"Kaj pomeni ta Wear this? A to si jaz samo označim ali gre to kam naprej?"` / **Eva (`eva3.mp4` `28:16`):** `"Jaz bi videla rada, da mogoče prvo stran ni tako, da ti vrže kar en outfit."`
findings.current: Tapping `"Wear this"` toggles the button label to `"Wearing today"` without explaining what it does, and launching the app immediately shows a single random outfit card on `Today`.
findings.expected: Clarify what `"Wear this"` does (logs wear history and prevents repeating the same outfit tomorrow) and revisit the `Today` home page layout so it feels more intentional.

findings.title: Redundant secondary `"All"` filter pills (`All 245`, `All 22`) in `Wardrobe`
findings.evidence: **Eva (`02:46`):** `"Zdaj ko grem na Clothing, mi spet vrže All... zakaj rabim še enkrat All? Če sem že na All 313, pa kliknem Clothing, zakaj mi spet pokaže All 245?"` / **Eva (`05:25`):** `"spet All izredno nepomemben"`
findings.current: Selecting a top-level category (`Clothing 246`, `Shoes 22`, `Accessories 46`) spawns a second row of pills starting with another `"All <count>"` pill selected by default.
findings.expected: Remove the redundant secondary `"All"` pill (superseded by the broader decision to replace horizontal pills with a visual category drill-down in `F-05`).

findings.title: Replace flat horizontal category pills in `Wardrobe` with a 2-level visual category drill-down (ABOUT YOU style)
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva3.mp4` `11:46`–`12:15`):** `"Takoj ko jaz odprem moj Wardrobe, bi jaz rada imela tole. Takole: da se mi naredi Oblačila, pa se mi da en kos oblačila, Šport, Obutev, Dodatki. Štiri kategorije bi rada imela. In potem, ko jaz kliknem na Oblačila, se mi pojavijo nove kategorije... In potem, ko jaz kliknem na Jakne, se mi šele pojavijo kosi!"`
findings.current: Opening `Wardrobe` immediately shows all 313 pieces under a flat horizontal scrolling strip of 18+ subcategory pills (`Tops & T-shirts`, `Shirts & blouses`, ..., `Loungewear & nightwear`).
findings.expected: Replace the horizontal pill bar and immediate `All 313` dump with an e-commerce-style visual category hierarchy: Level 1 shows 4 main category cards with a representative item thumbnail (`Clothing`, `Sport`, `Shoes`, `Accessories`); tapping a main category opens Level 2 visual subcategory cards with item thumbnails; tapping a subcategory opens the 2-column item grid with a floating `Filter` button.

findings.title: Only display populated categories in `Wardrobe` (progressive disclosure as wardrobe grows)
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`12:16`):** `"In ti bi imela samo tiste kategorije — jaz prikažem — za katere imaš cunje. Če bo recimo nekdo, ki ne bo imel nič cunj... bo samo napisalo 'Dodaj stvari v garderobo'. In potem, ko bo dodal recimo prve hlače, se mu bo pokazala kategorija 'Hlače'"` / **Eva (`12:38`):** `"Ja!"`
findings.current: Empty categories can appear in pickers or filter bars without progressive empty-state onboarding.
findings.expected: Only render categories and subcategories in `Wardrobe` for which the user has at least 1 piece; show an `"Add items to wardrobe"` empty state when 0 pieces exist.

findings.title: Dark-grey square card backgrounds in dark mode (`"te sivi kvadratki"`) and single-theme preference
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`05:31`):** `"A to je tak sivo ozadje za čevljem? To ni dobro, a?"` / **Eva (`07:07`–`07:28`):** `"Jaz mislim, da bi bilo čisto kul, če si ne rabi noben nastavljat... če bi bilo eno, ker imaš potem tudi slog aplikacije isti. Samo te sivi kvadratki, če grejo stran, bo top."`
findings.current: On Android with OS dark mode enabled, wardrobe grid cards render as dark-grey squares against a black page background, whereas the item detail view has a pure black background.
findings.expected: Remove the muddy grey square card backgrounds in the grid and use a single consistent app theme (preferably clean/light) across devices rather than building a theme switcher.

findings.title: Legacy imported item cutouts flipped 180° upside down (bikini tops and dress)
findings.evidence: **Eva (`09:06`):** `"Vse sem isto obrnjeno slikala in kar nekatere modrce mi je okoli obrnilo"` / **Eva (`16:49`):** `"Drugače glej, tole tudi Bodysuit je oblekica, ki mi jo je narobe obrnil"` `[Screen: White bikini top at 09:21 and red sleeveless dress under Bodysuits at 16:26 are upside down.]`
findings.current: Several items imported from the previous app version (bikini tops and a red mini dress) are stored flipped 180° upside down, which also caused the AI to misclassify the upside-down red dress as a `Bodysuit`.
findings.expected: Fix/re-orient upside-down item images and provide a rotation control in the item Edit screen so users can rotate misoriented cutouts.

findings.title: Widespread AI garment categorization errors across `Tops & T-shirts`, `Trousers`, `Bodysuits`, `Bags`, `Hats`, and `Shoes`
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva.styld1.mp4` `15:40`–`16:13`):** `"če greva samo po topih, ko imam 48 topov, od tega je 1, 2, 3... trije so modrci v bistvu, eno je šal, pa 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — pet jih moram prestavit pod športne stvari"` / **Eva (`19:45`–`20:00`):** `"pod Accessories: okej, Bags — evo, obroč mi je isto vrglo pod Bags, mojo kapo z rokavicami je isto vrglo pod Bags, nogavice mi je vrglo pod Bags, trak za lase mi je vrglo pod Bags"` / **Eva (`eva3.mp4` `31:30`):** `"In tudi predlagal mi je pižamo. To je spodnji del pižame."`
findings.current: Out of 49 items in `Tops & T-shirts`, 10 (~20%) were misclassified (4 bikini pieces, 5 sportswear tops, 1 scarf); red ski pants were in `Trousers`; striped pajama pants were in `Trousers`; an upside-down dress was in `Bodysuits`; a lapel pin was in `Hats`; and at least 8 non-bag items (3 pairs of gloves/mittens, 3 headbands, 1 hood-hat with mittens, 1 pair of Nike socks) were dumped into `Bags`. Primarily black Sorel snow boots were also tagged as `"black and beige boots"`.
findings.expected: Audit and re-run the AI categorization pipeline (and color detection), stop using `Bags` or `Tops & T-shirts` as fallback buckets, and properly classify swimwear, sportswear, loungewear/pajamas, scarves, gloves, socks, and hair accessories.

findings.title: Edit piece screen: users confuse the `Name` text input with the `What it is` category selector
findings.evidence: **Eva (`11:40`):** `"Ne morem spremenit kategorije! Na Bikini lahko samo ime spremenim."` `[Screen: At 11:18–11:27 Eva types "Bikini" into the "Name" input and clicks Save; the item stays in Tops & T-shirts with title "Bikini" until Kristjan tells her to scroll down to "What it is -> Swimwear" at 11:45–12:07.]`
findings.current: On the Edit piece form, `Name` is the first field at the top (defaulting to generic category names like `"Top"`), while `What it is` (category pills) sits below, causing Eva to edit `Name` when trying to change the category.
findings.expected: Make category selection (`What it is`) visually distinct and unmistakable from `Name` on the Edit form.

findings.title: Hide item name/category text labels below thumbnails in the `Wardrobe` grid
findings.evidence: **Eva (`12:24`, `13:15`):** `"Ta ime cunje ful nima smisla... Jaz mogoče tudi ne bi, da se mi ime pokaže, ampak bi raje videla, da se mi ime pokaže pol ko kliknem... ko si v garderobi vidiš samo slikico pa nič drugega."`
findings.current: Every card in the `Wardrobe` grid displays a text label underneath the cutout image (`Top`, `Swimwear`, `Bag`, `Bikini`).
findings.expected: Remove text labels from underneath item cards in the `Wardrobe` grid (show only the clean item cutout thumbnails) and display the item `Name` only on the piece detail view.

findings.title: Expand footwear & accessories taxonomy + support AI-created and user-created custom categories
findings.evidence: **Eva (`19:02`–`19:42`):** `"Vsaj te superge bi si jaz ločila, da imam športne čevlje vsaj pod 'Sport shoes'... 4 pari od teh superg, ki so tukaj navedeni, so vsi: eni so za tečt, eni so za dvoranske športe, eni so pa pohodniški"` / **Kristjan (`20:10`–`20:35`):** `"eno je razširit mogoče te osnovne kategorije, pa AI-ju dat mogoče malo svobode, da se sam odloči, ko skenira nekaj novega, pa če ni ta prave kategorije, da jo pač ustvari, in pa da še uporabniku dovolim, da si naredi svoje kategorije."`
findings.current: `Shoes` only shows `Trainers`, `Boots`, `Sandals` (mixing running/court/hiking shoes into `Trainers` and snow/hiking boots into `Boots`, and lacking `Loafers`, `Oxfords`, `Mary Janes`, `Ballet flats`, `Heels`). `Accessories` lacks `Gloves`, `Socks`, and `Hair accessories / Headbands`. Users cannot add custom categories.
findings.expected: (1) Expand base categories (`Sport shoes`, `Snow/Hiking boots`, `Loafers`, `Oxfords`, `Mary Janes`, `Ballet flats`, `Heels`; `Gloves`, `Socks`, `Hair accessories`), (2) allow the AI to create a new subcategory when scanning an item that doesn't fit presets, and (3) allow users to create/edit custom categories.

findings.title: Back navigation (`<`) from piece detail resets active `Wardrobe` category filter to `All 313`
findings.evidence: **Eva (`17:56`–`18:08`):** `"tudi to me moti, da ko jaz grem ven iz nekega čevlja — glej, če grem na Sandals — me pol namesto da bi me vrglo nazaj na čevlje, me vrže nazaj na vse cunje!"` / **Kristjan (`18:10`–`18:37`):** `"ko ti izbereš ta nek filter, se mora ta izbran filter zapisat v URL, in potem ko se premikaš nazaj, mora to v URL-ju ostat."`
findings.current: Filtering `Wardrobe` (e.g., `Shoes -> Sandals`), opening an item detail view, and tapping `<` Back resets `Wardrobe` to `All 313` instead of returning to `Shoes -> Sandals`.
findings.expected: Persist active category/subcategory filter state in URL search params (or route path) so back navigation preserves the active filter and scroll position.

findings.title: Android file picker on `"Add a photo"` in `Gallery` offers `My Files` (raw filenames) instead of opening photo gallery directly
findings.evidence: **Eva (`22:13`–`22:31`):** `"A je tle kakšna možnost, da jaz ne bi dobila takega, ker da bi dobila direkt iz galerije? Ker tle recimo zdaj jaz vidim samo po imenu..."` / **Kristjan (`22:58`):** `"Bom vprašal Clauda, zakaj to tako naredi."`
findings.current: Tapping `"Add a photo"` on Android Chrome triggers `Choose an action: Camera | My Files | Files`; picking `My Files` shows unpreviewable raw filenames (`20261102_153423.jpg`).
findings.expected: Configure the HTML `<input type="file" accept="image/*">` attributes so Android opens the visual photo picker / gallery directly when possible.

findings.title: Slow `"Finding the clothes..."` processing on Gallery photo uploads (~33s–45s)
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`24:53`):** `"Kar dolgo časa tole melje, se mi zdi."` `[Screen: Photo 1 takes ~33s (`23:35`–`24:08`) and Photo 4 takes ~64s (`31:47`–`32:51`) in "Finding the clothes...".]`
findings.current: Uploading a photo to `Gallery` stays in `"Finding the clothes..."` for 33 to 64 seconds.
findings.expected: Optimize the Gallery garment detection / cutout pipeline to reduce wait times and run cutout + detection together automatically.

findings.title: Gallery `"What you're wearing"` fails to detect worn pieces and fails to match items already in the user's wardrobe
findings.evidence: **Eva (`24:15`):** `"Vse je v garderobi: čevlji, pulover in majica [in plašč]."` / **Eva (`32:41`):** `"tle so in torbica, in čevlji, in oblekica je noter."` / **Eva (`34:16`):** `"Zdaj je to dodalo v mojo garderobo. Ampak to je že v moji garderobi, Kristjan! To ni v redu"`
findings.current: Across multiple uploaded photos where Eva is wearing items already in her wardrobe (coat, pullover, shirt, shoes, brown bag, black sandals, patterned dress), Styld detects only 1–2 items and marks every single one as `"Not in your wardrobe yet"` instead of matching existing pieces.
findings.expected: Improve multi-garment extraction and wardrobe similarity matching so existing wardrobe items are automatically linked (or suggested as top matches) rather than defaulting to `"Not in your wardrobe yet"`.

findings.title: Dark/black items render as white/light-grey inverted cutouts in Gallery and Board `Your pieces` strip
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`25:18`):** `"Kaj je tole, nekaj čudnega je tole ven izrezal, zakaj je bele barve?"` / **Eva (`25:49`):** `"Po obliki ga vidim, da je to ta plašč, samo ne vem, zakaj je take barve."` / **Eva (`29:54`):** `"Aja, mogoče mi črne stvari pobarva na belo, da jih kao boljše [vidiš]"`
findings.current: In Gallery (`2 Nov`), Eva's dark brown suede coat is cut out as a white/light-grey ghost silhouette (and even the linked wardrobe thumbnail next to `Coat` renders white/grey, while the actual wardrobe piece in `Coats 8` is dark brown). In the Board editor's `Your pieces` strip (`29:54`), dark/black garments also appear inverted/white.
findings.expected: Fix the image cutout/rendering pipeline and dark-mode CSS filters so dark brown and black garments retain their true dark colors and are never inverted to white/grey.

findings.title: Gallery `"What you're wearing"` detects random background bystanders instead of the user in the foreground
findings.evidence: **Eva (`27:13`):** `"Tle pa sploh ni zaznal mene, ampak je zaznal tega tipa od zadaj! In je zaznal majico in hlače!"` / **Eva (`30:43`–`30:55`):** `"Zaznal je tega starega dedka ... pa zaznal je to punco za mano!"` / **Kristjan (`30:53`):** `"Ampak moje punce pa ni zaznal!"`
findings.current: In two separate photos (carnival photo at `27:08` and Oktoberfest photo at `30:36`), the AI ignores Eva in the foreground and extracts the clothes of random people in the background (a man's black shirt/pants; an older man's lilac shirt with suspenders + white lederhosen and a background woman's dirndl).
findings.expected: Anchor `"What you're wearing"` person/garment detection strictly on the primary foreground subject (the user) and ignore background bystanders.

findings.title: Remove the intermediate Board overview screen (`Pinned` list + `Make with Styld` header) and open the interactive collage editor directly
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`28:42`):** `"on je kar dva koraka naredil... Tukaj v bistvu Board je že ta kolaž, mora biti, a ne."` / **Eva (`39:44`–`40:09`):** `"Pol ne rabim tega, mene lahko vrže direktno na ono, ne rabim tega! ... Bi bilo pa kul, da me direkt vrže na editing."` / **Kristjan (`40:11`):** `"Exactly."`
findings.current: Opening a board (or clicking `"Open"` after `"Save to board"`) lands on a read-only intermediate screen with a cropped preview, `"Make with Styld"`, `"Edit"`, `"Edit collage"`, and a `"Pinned"` grid below; saved items only appear in `"Pinned"` and must be manually tapped again inside `"Edit collage"` to appear on the canvas.
findings.expected: Eliminate the intermediate Board overview / `"Pinned"` screen; opening a board (or saving an item to a board) should open the interactive collage canvas directly with added items placed directly on the canvas.

findings.title: Replace unfiltered horizontal `Your pieces` strip in Board collage editor with a filterable `Add your piece` (`+`) bottom-sheet drawer
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva.styld1.mp4` `29:03`):** `"Tudi tlele spet v 'Your pieces', sorry ampak mi je ful smotano, da moram jaz tle zdaj čez vse svoje stvari it. Tle tudi rabim filtre..."` / **Kristjan (`29:12`–`29:41`):** `"da bi kliknila recimo tukajle gumb 'Add your piece', pa bi se ti od spodaj tak slider gor pripeljal, pa bi imela na vrhu filtre"` / **Eva:** `"Ja."`
findings.current: At the bottom of the Board collage editor, `Your pieces` displays all 313 wardrobe items in a single unfiltered horizontal scrolling row.
findings.expected: Replace the inline `Your pieces` horizontal strip with an `"Add your piece"` (`+`) button that opens a bottom-sheet drawer with category filters so users can quickly filter and tap items onto the canvas.

findings.title: Back button (`<`) in `To review` (`Open the review tray`) resets navigation to `Wardrobe -> Pieces` instead of returning to `Gallery`
findings.evidence: **Eva (`33:25`):** `"takoj ko grem nazaj, me vrže čisto na začetek"` / **Kristjan (`33:31`):** `"Spet mora, ohraniti si mora, če si bila v galeriji pa greš nazaj, da je spet nazaj v galeriji. To mora tako, da se v link shrani"`
findings.current: Tapping `<` Back from `To review | Styld` after opening it from a Gallery photo detail view sends the user to `Wardrobe -> Pieces` instead of returning to the Gallery photo.
findings.expected: Preserve the return URL/route when navigating to `To review` so pressing `<` Back returns to the originating Gallery photo.

findings.title: Adding a detected piece from a Gallery photo to Wardrobe requires too many clicks via the Review Tray
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`34:10`):** `"Tukaj se mi zdi, da je preveč klikanja, to bi moglo kar vse biti ..."` `[Screen: Tapping "Add to wardrobe" changes status to "Waiting in your review tray" -> user must tap "Open the review tray" -> tap "Add 1 to my wardrobe".]`
findings.current: Tapping `"Add to wardrobe"` on a detected garment in Gallery puts it in `"Waiting in your review tray"`, requiring 2 additional screens/clicks to actually add it.
findings.expected: Streamline `"Add to wardrobe"` from Gallery so it adds directly (or with a single inline confirmation) without routing through a separate Review Tray screen.

findings.title: `"Delete"` piece action is missing from the Edit piece screen (`pencil` icon)
findings.evidence: **Eva (`34:25`–`34:56`):** `"Deletat? ... Edit ... Ja, saj grem dol. ... Kje? ... Delete, tle! To je Delete this item, aha."` `[Screen: Eva twice opens Edit mode and scrolls to the bottom looking for Delete, where only Save and Cancel exist; Delete is only visible on the read-only detail view.]`
findings.current: Users who tap the top-right Edit pencil icon to delete a piece only find `"Save"` and `"Cancel"` at the bottom of the edit form; `"Delete"` is hidden at the bottom of the read-only view.
findings.expected: Include `"Delete"` inside the Edit piece view (as well as or instead of the read-only view) so users entering Edit mode to remove an item can find it immediately.

findings.title: Reduce button clutter on Gallery photo detail; make `"Favourite"` a heart icon overlaid on the photo
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`35:40`):** `"tukaj se mi zdi, da je malo preveč gumbov. Tale 'Favourite' gumb bi lahko mogoče bil samo srček na sami sliki recimo, a ne?"` / **Eva (`35:50`):** `"Ja."`
findings.current: Gallery photo detail displays 5 action buttons below the photo (`"Wear it again"`, `"Cut out the outfit"`, `"Favourite"`, `"Delete photo"`, `"Save to board"`).
findings.expected: Replace the `"Favourite"` text pill button with a heart icon overlaid directly on the photo to reduce button clutter.

findings.title: Auto-generate outfit cutout on Gallery photos and allow swiping left/right between original photo and cutout
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`eva.styld1.mp4` `35:57`, `37:46`):** `"Pa ta 'Cut out the outfit', to bi lahko kar avtomatsko naredilo ... Pač levo pa desno in pol imaš originalno sliko pa cut-out, in potem bi lahko vsaka od teh bila 'Add to board'."` / **Eva (`37:44`):** `"Da bi lahko tle se premikala med slikami, to bi bilo dobro, ja."`
findings.current: Users must manually click `"Cut out the outfit"`, and once cut out, the board only receives the cutout (`"The outfit is cut out; a board gets it on its own"`).
findings.expected: Automatically cut out the user's outfit when a photo is added to Gallery; let the user swipe left/right between the full original photo and the isolated outfit cutout (and between Gallery photos), and allow adding either version to a Board.

findings.title: Tapping `+` on `Boards` immediately creates blank `"My board"` records instead of opening a Board Template chooser
findings.evidence: **Eva (`38:49`):** `"da ko jaz kliknem na 'Boards', ta plusek meni da 'Make with Styld' template, ne da rabim pol še dvakrat klikniti."` / **Eva (`42:28`):** `"ko jaz stopim na 'Boards', bi kliknila na plus, in na plusu se bi mi prikazalo, tako kakor v PowerPointu, 'Templates'"`
findings.current: Tapping `+` on the `Boards` screen immediately creates an empty board named `"My board"` (leaving multiple empty `"My board (0 pins)"` cards in the list) and requires clicking `"Make with Styld"` inside it.
findings.expected: Tapping `+` on `Boards` should open a template selection screen (`Templates`) directly instead of creating an empty `"My board"` first.

findings.title: Add a Share button on the Board / collage view
findings.evidence: **Kristjan (`40:18`):** `"Pa potem tukajle bi tudi moral biti nek gumb za sharat."` / **Eva (`40:24`):** `"Ja"`
findings.current: The board view header (`< All boards`, `Make with Styld`, `Edit`) has no direct Share button.
findings.expected: Add a clear Share button on the board view so users can share their boards/collages.

findings.title: Android system Back button loops through intermediate board/editor history states
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva.styld1.mp4` `40:24`):** `"tukaj bi moral biti en gumb, da me ne vrže nazaj na... Glej, zdaj moram jaz vse..."` / **Kristjan (`eva3.mp4` `08:24`):** `"saj gumb obstaja, saj mora delati, no, če je gumb na Androidu, je na Androidu."`
findings.current: Pressing the Android hardware/gesture Back button cycles repeatedly back and forth between the collage editor, board overview, and modals instead of cleanly exiting to the parent list.
findings.expected: Fix browser history management (use `replaceState` for editor/modal sub-states and remove the intermediate board screen) so the Android system Back button exits cleanly.

findings.title: `"Make with Styld"` mood board AI selects inappropriate items (satin wedding dresses, bikini top, sports bra for `"Trip to India"`) and dumps 6 isolated pieces instead of complete outfits
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva.styld1.mp4` `42:09`):** `"...pač navadne zbralo cunje iz moje garderobe. By the way, dve od teh sta satenaste obleke, ki nimata kaj delat v Indiji. To so fancy obleke za, pač, poroke in tako. In nekaj je moj modrc iz kopalk. In nekaj je moj športni modrc."` / **Eva (`stly.eva2.mp4` `03:12`):** `"če se mi pokažejo samo takole kosi — kaj bom s tem? To mi nič ne pomaga, ne. Kar jaz rabim, je dejanske outfite"`
findings.current: Prompting `"Trip to india"` in `Make with Styld -> A mood board` simply placed 6 isolated green/cream items in a 2×3 grid on a dark background—including 2 formal satin wedding dresses, 1 bikini top, and 1 sports bra—matched purely by color rather than occasion or outfit structure.
findings.expected: AI board generation must assemble **complete multi-piece outfits** (top/layering, bottom, shoes, 1–3 accessories) appropriate for the requested occasion/weather, rather than dropping 6 isolated garments onto a grid.

findings.title: Board Template 1: `"One piece, six outfits"` (hero piece in center surrounded by 6–8 complete outfits + auto-cutout for store screenshots)
findings.evidence: **Eva (`eva3.mp4` `00:52`–`02:21`):** `"ko jaz pač zberem ta board, me vpraša, kateri kos mojih oblačil oziroma sliko hočem... Če bi sliko iz interneta vnesla, me vpraša, če hočem cutout... Če pa je iz moje garderobe, pa že ta obrezano stvar da takole na sredino... In potem okoli tega sestavi outfite. In sicer vsak outfit mora imeti čevlje, vsaj en dodatek — po možnosti dva vsaj — am, potem pa kos, ki ga izbereva, nek jopič, neko majico oziroma nek zgornji del... in spodnji del."`
findings.current: No guided `"One piece, six outfits"` template exists.

tickets.originalTitle: Fix broken `Add clothes` (`"Hold pieces up"` & `"Lay pieces out"`) Front/Back guided scanner, black-frame auto-captures, and background/body clothing segmentation (`F-48`, `F-51`)
tickets.body:
- **Priority**: **P0** — Eva explicitly concluded `"Tako da ta funkcija ne deluje"` (`"So this function does not work"`) after 4 consecutive tests: the guided scanner fails to attach `Back` photos to `Front` pieces (creating 2–3 separate duplicate `"Top"` items in `Wardrobe` or saving the front image into both `Front` and `Back` slots), auto-captures pitch-black frames when the phone rests on the bed (`"Trousers / Top — Needs a better look"`), and cuts out the user's own worn clothes and background closet coats (`14 pieces found` for 3 held-up items).
- **Affected Routes & UI Components**:
  - `Add clothes | Styld` -> Guided camera modes (`"Hold pieces up — Your camera takes each one"` and `"Lay pieces out — Your camera takes each one from above"`)
  - Camera state machine: top pill toggle (`Front` | `Back`), bottom instruction pill (`"Hold one piece up, then keep still"` / `"Lay one piece flat, then take your hands away"` -> `"Now show its back, or tap the picture"` / `"Now turn it over, or tap the picture"`), `"Skip the back"` button, `"Looking..."` badge, `"Got it. Show the next piece"` toast, `"N taken"` top-right counter, `"Done"` bottom-left button.
  - `To review | Styld` (`"N pieces found / They're cut out and ready. Untick anything that isn't yours."`, `"Finding pieces..."` cards, `"No clothes found in a photo. [Remove]"`, `"Add N to my wardrobe"` button).
  - `Wardrobe | Styld` piece detail view (`Front` | `Back` toggle pills vs. `"Add the back"` button).
- **Root Causes Observed on Screen (`eva5styld.mp4` `05:31`–`15:35`)**:
  1. **Broken `Front` + `Back` pairing in `To review` and `Wardrobe`**:
     - In Test 1 (`Hold pieces up`, `05:31`–`09:30`), Eva held up 3 garments (beige trousers, white buttoned top, white camisole top). `To review` ticked 5 items (`Add 5 to my wardrobe`): 1 `Trousers` item (where tapping `Front` and `Back` showed the **exact same front photo** because the second shutter fired before she finished turning the trousers) and **4 separate standalone `"Top"` items** (front of buttoned top, back of buttoned top, front of camisole, back of camisole—each saved as its own separate wardrobe piece with an `"Add the back"` button).
     - In Test 2 (`Hold pieces up`, `09:34`–`11:18`), Eva carefully scanned 1 cream buttoned top (`1 taken` on Front at `09:50`, then turned it around for `2 taken` on Back at `09:54`). Even though the camera UI stepped from `Front` to `Back`, `To review | Styld` (`10:35`) created **two separate checked `"Top"` cards** (`Add 2 to my wardrobe`), and saving added two separate `"Top"` pieces to `Wardrobe` (`All 320`), neither having a `Back` attached (`11:00`–`11:08`).
     - In Tests 3 & 4 (`Lay pieces out`, `13:03`–`15:35`), scanning 1 cream buttoned top flat on the bed again produced 2–3 separate `"Top"` cards in `To review` (`Add 2 to my wardrobe` at `13:54`, `Add 3 to my wardrobe` at `15:23`).
  2. **Pitch-black camera frames auto-captured when phone is set down on the bed**:
     - In `"Lay pieces out"`, the user needs both hands to flip the garment and arrange it neatly on the bed, so she sets the phone face-down on the bedsheet (`13:07`–`13:12`, `13:20`–`13:24`, `14:15`–`14:28`, `14:42`–`14:48`).
     - Because a phone resting on a bed is completely still (`0` motion delta between frames), the stillness detector immediately triggers `"Looking..."` and auto-captures a pitch-black photo (`"2 taken"` at `13:22`, `"3 taken"` at `14:44`).
     - Worse, this black frame **advances the `Front`/`Back` state machine** (consuming the `Back` slot so the actual back photo is captured as the `Front` of a new piece!) tickets.originalTitle: Audit and fix AI garment categorization, color tagging, and upside-down legacy cutouts across Wardrobe (`F-08`, `F-09`)
tickets.body:
- **Priority**: **P0** — Core AI recommendations (`Today`, `Ask Styld`, and `Boards`) are actively broken because ~20% of tops, 8/22 bags, ski pants, and pajama bottoms are misclassified (causing Styld to recommend striped pajama pants, snow boots, and formal wedding dresses for everyday/travel looks).
- **Specific Misclassifications & Orientation Bugs Observed (`eva.styld1.mp4` `09:05`–`20:37`, `eva3.mp4` `30:55`–`33:25`)**:
  1. **180° Upside-Down Cutouts**:
     - Multiple bikini tops in `Swimwear` (`09:06`–`09:38`, e.g., white bandeau bikini top with tie straps pointing downward in `fig05a`) and a red sleeveless mini dress (`16:23`–`16:57`, `fig06`) are stored upside-down (180° rotated). Because the red dress is upside down, the AI classifier misidentified its skirt hem + straps as a `Bodysuit` (`Bodysuits 1`).
  2. **`Tops & T-shirts 49` (~20% error rate)**:
     - Out of 49 items in `Tops & T-shirts`, Eva counted **10 misclassified items**: 4 bikini tops (`Swimwear`), 5 gym/sport tops (`Sportswear`), and 1 knit scarf (`Scarves`).
  3. **`Trousers 29` (ski pants & pajamas mixed into everyday trousers)**:
     - Red waterproof ski trousers (`15:19`) were placed in `Trousers` instead of `Sportswear`.
     - Light-blue and white striped drawstring pajama bottoms (`eva3.mp4` `30:55`–`31:58`, `fig21b`, `fig21c`) were classified as everyday `Trousers` instead of `Loungewear & nightwear`, causing `Ask Styld` (`"What should I wear today?"`) to recommend wearing striped pajama bottoms with a brown coat and snow boots!
  4. **`Accessories -> Bags 22` (used as a fallback dump bucket)**:
     - 8 non-bag items were dumped into `Bags`: 3 pairs of winter mittens/gloves (e.g., grey fingerless gloves in row 1 col 3 of `fig01`), 3 hairbands/headbands (`obroč`, `trak za lase`), 1 knit hood-hat with attached mittens, and 1 pair of white Nike crew socks.
     - Under `Hats 16`, a tiny decorative lapel pin/brooch was classified as a `Hat` (`20:08`).
  5. **Color Tagging Error on Footwear**:
     - Sorel winter snow boots that are ~90% black with a thin white/beige rubber sole trim (`eva3.mp4` `31:05`, visible in `fig21c` carousel right edge) were tagged and described by AI as `"black and beige boots"`.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Add orientation detection/correction in the cutout pipeline (and a manual `Rotate 90°/180°` button in the piece Edit screen) and fix upside-down cutouts in the wardrobe dataset.
  - [ ] Re-run/upgrade the garment classifier prompt & schema so `Bags` and `Tops & T-shirts` are never used as catch-all fallback buckets; accurately route swimwear/bikini tops to `Swimwear`, gym/ski gear to `Sportswear`, pajama bottoms to `Loungewear & nightwear`, scarves to `Scarves`, and gloves/socks/headbands to their proper `Accessories` subcategories.
  - [ ] Weight primary color extraction by garment surface area so small sole trims or logos do not override the dominant garment color.

tickets.originalTitle: Fix Gallery person & garment detection to target the foreground user, auto-match existing wardrobe pieces, and stop inverting dark items to white (`F-16`, `F-17`, `F-18`)

- **Priority**: **P0** — The `Gallery` feature is currently unusable in testing because it extracts clothing from random background bystanders instead of Eva in the foreground, turns her dark brown suede coat and black items into white ghost cutouts, and fails to link items that already exist in her wardrobe.

     - Increase the post-capture cooldown / stillness grace period so the user has time to flip the garment, and once stillness is confirmed, display a **large, high-contrast `"3"`, `"2"`, `"1"` numeric countdown overlay in the center of the camera viewport** ("like in a video game before you start") before firing the shutter.
  2. **Clearer Finish / Review Action (`F-50`)**:

Eva immediately tapped `"Photos or a video"` expecting the guided camera, which opened Android's native camera without framing guides.

tickets.body:

tickets.originalTitle: Build the `"One piece, six outfits"` and `"Wishlist board"` guided Board Templates (with auto-cutout for store screenshots and complete multi-piece outfits) (`F-26`, `F-29`, `F-30`, `F-31`, `F-32`, `F-33`)
tickets.body:
- **Priority**: **P1** — Agreed as the highest "wow effect" priority for `Boards`: tapping `+` on `Boards` should open a template picker where choosing `"One piece, six outfits"` or `"Wishlist board"` places a central hero/wishlist piece (auto-cutting out store screenshots) and generates 6–8 complete outfits (top/layers, bottom, shoes, 1–3 accessories) around it on a thematic background instead of dropping 6 isolated garments.
- **Detailed Product & Engineering Spec (`eva.styld1.mp4` `40:48`–`46:13`; `stly.eva2.mp4` `00:10`–`03:56`; `eva3.mp4` `00:38`–`07:50`)**:
  1. **Tapping `+` on `Boards` Opens Template Chooser (`F-26`)**:
     - Do not create a blank `"My board (0 pins)"` record when `+` is tapped. Instead, open a `"Templates"` chooser screen (`"like in PowerPoint"`).
  2. **Every AI-Generated Board Must Consist of Complete Outfits (`F-29`)**:
     - Never output 6 isolated single garments in a grid (like `"Trip to india"` in `fig12`, which selected 2 formal satin wedding dresses, 1 bikini top, and 1 sports bra just because they were green/cream).
     - Every generated outfit cluster on a board must be a **complete, wearable outfit** appropriate for the occasion and weather:
       - Top + layering piece (cardigan, blazer, sweater, jacket, or coat when appropriate; up to 2–3 upper layers like t-shirt + sweater + coat)
       - Bottom (trousers, jeans, skirt, shorts—unless the base is a dress/jumpsuit)
       - Shoes (`1 pair`)
       - Accessories (`at least 1–2, up to 3`: bag, sunglasses, belt, hat, scarf, or jewellery)
  3. **Template 1 (Build First — Highest "Wow Effect"): `"One piece, six outfits"` (`F-30`, `F-33`, `fig14`, `fig15`, `fig17`)**:
     - **Input**: Prompts the user to pick **1 piece from their `Wardrobe`** OR **upload an external photo/screenshot** (if external, ask if they want to cut it out / auto-cutout the background).
     - **Layout**: Places the hero piece in the center (as in `fig14` / `fig15`) or repeats the exact same hero cutout in the same orientation inside each of 6–8 outfit clusters around the board (`fig17`).
     - **Dynamic Visual Composition & Thematic Background (`F-33`)**: Vary the relative positions of shoes, bags, and accessories across the 6–8 outfit clusters so the board looks like a curated editorial collage rather than a rigid spreadsheet, and automatically select a complementary thematic background color (`Paper`, e.g., warm beige, soft light blue for a black-and-white polka-dot dress, etc.) instead of black.
  4. **Template 2: `"Wishlist board"` (`F-31`, `fig16`)**:
     - **Input**: Shows an `"Add a wishlist item"` button where the user uploads a screenshot or photo of an item from an online store they are thinking of buying (e.g., green Adidas Gazelle sneakers from ABOUT YOU in `fig16`).
     - **Behavior**: Automatically removes the background from the store screenshot, places the wishlist item in the center of the board, and generates 6 complete outfits around it using pieces **from the user's existing wardrobe** so the user can see if they already own enough matching clothes to justify buying the item.
  5. **Template 3: `"Seven outfits of a week"` / `"My trip"` (`F-32`, `fig18b`)**:
     - Prompts for destination/weather (e.g., `"What's the weather gonna be?"` -> `"cold December week"` or `"rainy September week"`) and arranges 7 complete multi-piece outfits in a clean grid (`fig18b`).
  6. **Template 4: `"Outfit of the day"` (`F-32`)**:
     - User types what they are doing today / the vibe, and AI lays out 1 complete outfit collage on the board.
  7. **Template 5: `"Blank"` Lookbook Template (`F-32`, `fig18a`)**:
     - Freeform canvas where the user can set a title (e.g., `"Office looks 2026"` or `"Best looks of 2026"`), pick a background color, arrange full-body outfit cutouts from their `Gallery` (`fig18a`), and share publicly.

tickets.originalTitle: Serve every remaining owner-only picture by signed address: board images, Gallery photos and their garments, `To review` detections and turns (follow-up to the 2 Nov D1 overload; relates to `F-43`, `T-14`)
tickets.body:
- **Priority**: **P1**. On 2 Nov the preview answered `"Kosov ni bilo mogoče naložiti"` and showed placeholder squares: every thumbnail made the Worker read the session and a D1 row, so a wardrobe page of 300+ pictures overloaded D1. Wardrobe pieces moved to signed addresses (`/cdn/media/…`, release `bf8f987`, live in `d73475c`). These still check the session and D1 per picture:
  - `GET /cdn/boards/images/:imageId/:size` (`packages/server/src/boards/Http.ts`)
  - `GET /cdn/photos/:photoId/:size` and `/cdn/photos/:photoId/garments/:garmentId` (`packages/server/src/photos/Http.ts`)
  - `GET /cdn/detections/:detectionId/:which` and `/cdn/turns/:pieceId/:which` (`packages/server/src/capture/Http.ts`)
  - MCP view thumbnails
- **Detailed Implementation Spec**:
  - Reuse `kernel/SignedMedia.ts` as is: grants over account, object, R2 key, content type, size, version and an hour-rounded expiry (+24 h), keyed from `AUTH_SECRET` under `styld-media-v1`. Do not add a second signer.
  - Each API that returns one of these entities returns its picture addresses already signed (`images` fields as on `Piece`). The web stops building them in `apps/web/src/Cdn.ts` (`boardImage`, `photo`, `photoGarment`, `detection`, `turn`), and those builders go.
  - The `/cdn/media` handler serves every kind: verify the signature, read R2, transform through Images where a size is asked, then the edge Cache API, with `private, immutable`. No session and no D1. The old per-kind routes are deleted, with no redirects.
  - Turn videos need `Range` support on the signed route (the `<video>` element seeks).
  - Version changes whenever the object may have changed (a redraw, a new cut-out, a re-found photo), so a cached copy is never shown for a new picture.
  - Board styles: `View.styles.ts` keys `mix-blend-mode` off the `/cdn/media/` prefix. Mark piece pictures by attribute instead, so board images keep their true colour once they share the route.
  - Assistants (MCP) still get no picture addresses. MCP Apps views load thumbnails through the view's own signed grant if they need them, never a session cookie.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - A board of 50+ pictures, a Gallery of 100+ photos and a `To review` tray of 30+ detections load with zero D1 queries per picture in Workers Logs, and no `D1 DB is overloaded`.
  - A tampered, expired or other-account address answers 403. A deleted object answers 404.
  - A redraw or new cut-out shows the new picture on the next list read, not the cached one.
  - A tab left open past the expiry recovers on its next list refresh, with no broken pictures.
  - Native: signed board, photo, detection and turn reads with no cookie. Preview readback of each kind.
- **Overhead**: one HMAC-SHA256 per address when a list is answered (native Web Crypto, the key derived once per isolate). That is microseconds per address, a few milliseconds for a 300-piece wardrobe. Serving costs one HMAC verify and no D1 or session read, and repeat views come from the edge cache. It is cheaper than today on both ends.
